mechanism_narrative: The recent stability in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT at depressed levels implies commuting demand is not recovering, so retail footfall should remain weak or soften further over the next month as weekday trips to shops stay constrained.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not recover from their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while WORKPLACES stays deeply negative, substitution toward home-based routines will keep discretionary retail trips suppressed and push RETAIL_REC lower within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 while WORKPLACES stays below -30 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above +5 and WORKPLACES remaining below -30.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT above its recent trough should translate into more in-person shopping trips with a short lag, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week as access friction falls.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by at least 3 points week-on-week from a sub -30 base
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points from below -30.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility is rising while GROCERY_PHARM is flat or falling, households are reallocating outings toward leisure and errands outside home, which should spill over into more retail visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS is above +10 and GROCERY_PHARM is below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean even though PARKS stays above +10 and GROCERY_PHARM stays below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in TRANSIT while WORKPLACES remains negative signals partial reopening without full office return; that combination should lift retail demand only after a brief lag as shoppers resume mixed-purpose trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises for two straight weeks while WORKPLACES stays below -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after two consecutive weekly gains in TRANSIT while WORKPLACES remains below -30.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent deterioration in GROCERY_PHARM alongside weak WORKPLACES indicates people are concentrating on essential trips and avoiding discretionary shopping, which should keep RETAIL_REC below the recent average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -25 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -25 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility falls from its current elevated level, that indicates more time spent outside the home and a higher willingness to make discretionary trips, which should nudge retail mobility upward within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL drops below +5 after holding above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL falls below +5.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling WORKPLACES and falling TRANSIT implies a renewed restriction or avoidance regime that directly suppresses shopping trips, so retail mobility should decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both turn down for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline for two consecutive weeks.
